title: Traffic fencing handoff with replay safeguard
author: Maya Rodriguez
description:
Context and motivation: We continue to see rare but high-impact partial promotions during multi-stage rollouts where in-flight sessions or transient backpressure cause a promoted cohort to observe diverging behavior. Earlier mitigations (shorter hold windows, noisy-metric smoothing) reduced incidence but did not provide a deterministic handoff path for sessions already in-flight. This PR introduces a traffic-fencing handoff state and a replay safeguard so that staged promotes either complete deterministically or can be rolled back and replayed to validate correctness before full promotion.

What this changes (summary): Adds a fencing state machine and a replay buffer adapter to the rollout conductor, wiring to metrics and tracing, test coverage, and a conservative default policy. The change is intentionally opt-in via rollout.policy.fencing.enabled=false to avoid altering current production rollouts until staged adoption. Key user-visible behaviors: 1) During a phased handoff, cohorts are fenced (new sessions routed using fence tokens), 2) in-flight sessions are tracked and quiesced to a consistent snapshot, 3) if anomaly gates trigger, the fence can be closed and the replay buffer used to simulate promotion offline before retry.

Implementation notes (high level): - New state: FENCE_OPEN -> FENCE_HOLD -> PROMOTE/REPLAY/ROLLBACK. - Fence token generation and propagation added to the API gateway routing layer (redwood-gateway) and the routing table. - Lightweight replay buffer persists ids + request prefixes + KV-cache footprints for up to 30 minutes; a replay adapter can replay traffic against a candidate model in a sandboxed backend. - Added metrics: rollout.fence.open_count, rollout.fence.quiesced_sessions, rollout.replay.success_rate, replay.latency_p95. - Safety defaults: fencing requires canary_success_ratio >= 0.98 for auto-promotion; otherwise operator-driven promote after manual verification.

Files changed (high level): - services/conductor/rollout_state_machine.go (adds fencing states and transition guards) - gateway/routing/fence_tokens.go (token lifecycle, propagation) - sandbox/replay/adapter.go (sandbox replay runner + KV footprint handling) - console/rollouts_ui/fence_modal.tsx (console control to inspect fence state + replays) - metrics/registrations.go (new metrics) - test/integration/fence_replay_test.go (end-to-end test covering quiesce+replay paths) - charts/values.yaml (flag to enable fencing and default TTLs)

Commits (summary): - 8f3b2d1: introduce fencing state machine and guard logic - 2d7c4a9: gateway token propagation and routing changes - b1f6e03: replay buffer implementation and sandbox runner - 4caa9e0: console UI for fence inspection and replay controls - 9eab447: metrics and tests + config flags - dff12a6: docblocks and rollout policy defaults

Review thread (condensed): - Connor Li (reviewer): "Overall strong. Please ensure the replay buffer cannot leak PII; add an explicit scrub step and a proof-of-concept scrub unit test." - Author (Maya): "Added request scrub hook and unit test (test/scrub_test.go). The scrub is pluggable and defaults to header and body key whitelist." - Priya Natarajan (SRE): "How does fencing interact with autoscaling? If we quiesce sessions for 30s we might spike memory on the host." - Author: "Fencing keeps only request prefixes and KV-cache footprints (not full responses). We also added a TTL and a memory cap per-host; when cap is reached the conductor will prioritize replay to disk and signal a 'deferred_replay' metric. Notes added to design doc." - Jasper Holt (SEC): "Confirm replay runs in a sandboxed network namespace with no egress to prod resources." - Author: "Replay runner is an isolated sandbox with strict egress rules. Added network isolation integration test in sandbox/replay/sandbox_test.go."

CI and test results: - Unit tests: pass - Integration tests (fence_replay_test) initially flaky on CI runner; rerun succeeded. - E2E smoke in staging: pass with two manual promotons. - Lint/format: pass. Overall ci_status: pass.

Backward compatibility and rollout: - Backwards compatible: fence tokens are optional; older gateways ignore unknown token headers. - Default is disabled; rollout via feature flag; we recommend enabling in a single region per-customer and monitoring rollout.fence.* metrics for 72h before global enabling.

Performance and cost: Replay buffer is bounded and uses an LRU spill-to-s3 path when per-host in-memory cap is reached. We measured a median additional memory of ~3.4MB/host for a 5-minute fence TTL in internal load test (see bench/notes).

Related work and Linear tickets: ENG-2140 (design), ENG-2311 (sandbox replay runner), ENG-2367 (gateway token work).

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals from Connor and Priya and an explicit security signoff from Jasper. Post-merge tasks: ship rollout policy docs and notify Platform SRE about the feature flag window.

Checklist: - [x] Design documentation updated - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Metrics and alerts added - [x] Console controls wired - [x] Security review

If you want to try this locally: enable rollout.policy.fencing.enabled=true in charts/values.local.yaml, deploy conductor + gateway, and run test/integration/fence_replay_test.go.
release_notes: Add opt-in traffic-fencing handoff with replay safeguard to improve deterministic promotions. Disabled by default; see rollout.policy.fencing.enabled.
